module.screenshot.checks: Takes a screenshot of the home page in a headless browser (Chromium), through the scan proxy if there is one.
module.screenshot.fix:
Open the screenshot and compare it with the page a visitor should see: logo, texts, language, layout. A blank page, an error message, a server welcome page or content you did not publish are signals to deal with.
If the content is unexpected (a hacker's message, advertising, a redirect, sale of drugs or gambling): treat the site as compromised. Put it behind a maintenance page right away, keep a copy of the logs, then restore a clean backup from before the intrusion.
After a compromise, change every related password and key (hosting, CMS, FTP or SSH, database), update the CMS, plugins and themes, delete unknown accounts and files, and fix the entry point before putting the site back online.
If it is a default page (for example "Welcome to nginx", "It works!", the IIS start page): publish your real site at the web server root, or remove this site if it is not needed, because a default install often leaves other settings to harden.
If it is a registrar parking page or an "under construction" page: the domain does not point to your site. Fix the `A`, `AAAA` or `CNAME` records in the DNS zone, or delete them if the name is no longer used.
A hacked site can show different content depending on the visitor (robot, mobile, country, arrival from a search engine): also compare with an ordinary browser, in a private window and from another network.
If the screenshot is missing (module "not applicable"): Playwright or its Chromium browser is not installed; run the first command in the snippet, then run the scan again. If the page does not respond, check with `curl -sIL` that the site is reachable, and check the proxy in Settings.
Keep the screenshot as a reference and compare it with each new scan, especially after a redesign or a change of host: any difference you did not intend must be explained.
module.screenshot.fix_snippet:
# Playwright
python -m playwright install --only-shell chromium
# curl
curl -sIL https://example.com/
module.screenshot.title: Screenshot
module.screenshot.why: Seeing the page as a visitor sees it helps spot a defacement, a default page or a parked domain.
